game.title: Mad Max
game.build_notes: Verified on Windows 10, 2026-09-03, with our dxgi.dll proxy present. Ran windowed at 784x561. Driven entirely by external synthetic input. Home PC 2026-09-04: windowed 1920x1080, same proxy; driven by the same harness with 0.25-0.3 s key holds. Dev PC 2026-09-04b: 784x561 windowed, staging 4533ec9 build, 0.25-0.3 s holds; full run incl. self-close.

api_notes: Standard primitives: scancodes, KEYEVENTF_EXTENDEDKEY for arrows, foreground first, BitBlt for capture.
The window title is exactly 'Mad Max'. NOTE the process owns several windows (DIEmWin, Default IME, MSCTFIME UI); match on the VISIBLE one.
The window does not exist for the first several seconds after launch - the process starts, then creates it. A find-window failure right after launch means 'still starting', not 'wrong title'.

PROBE HOTKEYS ARE NUMPAD AND NUMLOCK-INDEPENDENT: the cbfp probe reads GetAsyncKeyState and accepts either the numpad VK or the navigation VK (NUMPAD4 or LEFT = mark A, NUMPAD5 or CLEAR = mark B, NUMPAD3 or PGUP = dump). Send NON-EXTENDED scancodes 0x4B/0x4C/0x51 and it works whatever NumLock is set to.

HOLD DURATION MATTERS: 70 ms taps were ignored on the home PC at 1920x1080 (two Esc taps, screen unchanged, game rendering and focused) while 250-300 ms holds registered every time (~20 presses). Use `hold <key> 0.3`, not `key`. [verified-live 2026-09-04] The dev PC's 70 ms taps at 784x561 still stand as recorded there.

Focus BEFORE the first capture: an unfocused BitBlt returned the whole desktop (3424 px wide) around the window; every capture after focusing was the clean 1920x1080 client area. [verified-live 2026-09-04]

CAPTURE MODE'S SETTINGS TABS ARE MOUSE-ONLY: click the tab label, click a row label to select it, click the < / > arrows at the ends of its bar to change it. Keyboard Down/Right, clicking the bar, and dragging the knob all do nothing. game-harness.py has a `click <x> <y>` command (client coordinates) for this. [verified-live 2026-09-04b, dev PC]

KEYMAP DECODING: `Mad Max\settings.ini` [KeyMapping] stores alphabetical indices A=0..Z=25 (move_forward=22 W, move_left=0 A, move_backward=18 S, move_right=3 D live-verified; vehicle_fp_cam=21 V, enter_vehicle=exit_vehicle=17 R, overview_camera=23 X, action=4 E, cancel_action=16 Q inferred). Read it before guessing a key. [inferred-static 2026-09-04]

bindings.action: advance the title screen ('PRESS ANY BUTTON')

bindings.notes: Menus show 'NAVIGATE / SELECT' hints; Esc backs out.

bindings.action: Capture Mode: move / rotate / tilt / exit

keys.name: U = tilt left, I = tilt right
Esc = exit, Enter = capture image, R = video mode

bindings.notes: On-screen hints: MOVE / ROTATE / U TILT LEFT / I TILT RIGHT / Enter CAPTURE IMAGE / R VIDEO MODE / Esc EXIT. Tab switching (CAMERA / FILTERS / CAMERA SETTINGS / VIGNETTE) is NOT on arrows (they move the camera), E or Tab - untested: mouse on the chevrons, Q.

User-reported 2026-09-04 and config-backed (settings.ini vehicle_fp_cam = V). Pressed ON FOOT 2026-09-04b: nothing, as expected. IN-CAR PRESS STILL OWED: the early-story garage car is a non-enterable prop (user-confirmed), so a save past the first driving mission is needed. Check with the cbfp probe whether slot 9 / the main-pass matrix jump from the chase camera to the driver seat.
From settings.ini keymap_group_enter_vehicle=17 (=R). Pressed beside the early-story garage car with no effect - that car is a prop, so this is not a disproof.

bindings.action: Capture Mode: CAMERA SETTINGS tab, FIELD OF VIEW slider

keys.name: mouse click on tab label / row label / < > arrows

bindings.notes: At 784x561: CAMERA SETTINGS label (452,106); FIELD OF VIEW label (85,174); arrows (55,189) and (272,189). Each > click is ~3 deg of horizontal FOV near the default; range 58.3-116.9 deg hfov; resets when Capture Mode is left with Esc.

bindings.action: toggle the FIRST-PERSON COCKPIT camera while in a vehicle
bindings.notes: A SHIPPED first-person cockpit view - windscreen, steering wheel, dashboard - toggling cleanly back to the chase camera. Measured on slot 9, the frame-constant main camera: no-input control 0.00 units, V 6.76 units, V again 6.22 units back, second control 0.06 units, i.e. about a car length in opposite directions against essentially exact controls. The most VR-relevant control surface on this game, and it needs no code. Tested STATIONARY only - behaviour under motion is unknown.

R exits. It did NOT re-enter when Max had walked away, so entering needs proximity to the car - a probe that assumes R is a symmetric toggle will silently measure the player on foot instead, which is exactly what happened once on 2026-09-08.

steps: wait ~40s through the legal splash (the window may not exist for the first seconds)
Enter at the title screen
main menu appears with RESUME GAME already highlighted
Enter
wait ~60s for the world to load
Escape (pause menu, RESUME GAME highlighted)
Down x3 to EXIT TO MAIN MENU - VERIFY the highlight
Enter
confirm dialog: Enter = YES directly, Esc = NO (no navigation needed)
wait ~25s for the main menu
Down x7 to EXIT GAME - VERIFY, NEW GAME sits directly under RESUME GAME
Enter, then Enter to confirm
routes.notes: Process exits ~2s after the final confirm.

steps: Escape (pause menu, RESUME GAME highlighted)
Down x7 - the highlight SKIPS greyed rows (WASTELAND MISSIONS, ENCOUNTERS): RESUME > AUTOSAVES > SETTINGS > EXIT TO MAIN MENU > STORY MISSIONS > TUTORIALS > STATISTICS > CAPTURE MODE
VERIFY the highlight is on CAPTURE MODE (EXIT TO MAIN MENU is passed on the way)
Enter; the free camera is live in ~2 s
Esc returns to gameplay (not exercised this session)
routes.notes: The Capture Mode camera writes the same GlobalConstants slot 9 and main-pass matrix as gameplay (W for 1.5 s moved the eye 6.34 units along the view forward), so it is a valid testbed for camera-constant experiments.

steps: click the CAMERA SETTINGS tab label (452,106 at 784x561)
click the FIELD OF VIEW row label (85,174) - it highlights
click the > arrow (272,189) or < arrow (55,189) repeatedly; ~3 deg hfov per click
Esc leaves Capture Mode and resets the FOV
routes.notes: Coordinates are client-area pixels for the 784x561 window; scale them for other window sizes. Verified with the cbfp probe dumping after each change.

steps: R  (the Capture Mode HUD bar reads 'R VIDEO MODE')
click the CAMERA SETTINGS tab label - the tabs are MOUSE-ONLY
click the FIELD OF VIEW row label, then its '>' arrow repeatedly (18 clicks reaches maximum)
Enter  ('BEGIN SESSION')
Enter  ('CONTINUE' on the CAPTURE VIDEO panel)
-> live, playable, HUD-free gameplay at hfov ~157.4 degrees
routes.notes: Measured |col 0| = 0.2000 -> hfov ~157.4 deg, against an 80.48 deg gameplay default and a 116.91 deg Photo-Mode maximum. Two controllers are required and the game says so in its own UI twice; two ViGEm virtual pads (tools/hold-pads.py) satisfied it on a machine with zero physical pads, XInput slots [0,1]. NOT ESTABLISHED: that the pads were NECESSARY - no pads-removed control was run. Also unknown: how to end the session cleanly (Esc reaches the pause menu and RESUME GAME returns INTO the session).

console.notes: Not investigated. This project drives the game through its own dxgi.dll proxy, whose probes are triggered by numpad hotkeys and which writes madmax_vr_proxy_log.txt in the game folder.

capture_mode.notes: IS a free camera: arrows/WASD move, mouse rotates, U/I tilt, Enter captures, R video mode, Esc exits. Drives the same shared camera constant as gameplay. Tabs CAMERA / FILTERS / CAMERA SETTINGS / VIGNETTE exist; the key that switches them was not found (arrows, E, Tab tried). 2026-09-04b: tabs switch by MOUSE CLICK on the label (not a key). CAMERA SETTINGS has EXPOSURE / FIELD OF VIEW / BLUR INTENSITY / DOF FOCUS DISTANCE / DEPTH OF FIELD / AUTOFOCUS ON MAX; sliders change via their < > arrows. The FOV slider edits the main-pass projection columns only (58.3-116.9 deg hfov) and resets on Esc.

second_controller_camera.notes: A SHIPPED detached camera driven by a SECOND controller during live gameplay. The CAPTURE VIDEO panel documents: Increase/Decrease Field Of View, Attach/Detach Camera To Max, Toggle Game Camera, Toggle Camera Tracking, Toggle Alternate Camera 1, Toggle Alternate Camera 2, Rotate Camera Axis (two axes), Pan Up, Pan Down, Toggle Depth Of Field, Normal Game Speed, Slow Motion, Start/Stop Recording. The LIST is verified-live as documentation (read off the game's own panel 2026-09-08); every individual binding is REPORTED as behaviour because none has been pressed. Driving pad 1's buttons is the outstanding work - an engine-native attach/detach plus FOV pair would be a decoupled camera reachable with no code.

hazards.hazard: NEW GAME sits directly under RESUME GAME on the main menu
hazards.notes: Both the title menu default and the exit path pass by it. Navigate, capture, verify the highlight, then commit.

hazards.hazard: The window does not exist immediately after launch
hazards.notes: MadMax.exe appears in the process list several seconds before it creates its visible window. A find-window failure at that moment is a timing artefact, not a wrong title - retry rather than concluding the game did not start.

hazards.hazard: The process owns several non-game windows
hazards.notes: DIEmWin, Default IME (x2) and MSCTFIME UI all belong to MadMax.exe and are invisible. Filter on IsWindowVisible or you may attach to the wrong one.

hazards.hazard: Short synthetic taps can be silently ignored
hazards.notes: 70 ms scancode taps did nothing on the home PC while 250-300 ms holds worked every time. A key that does nothing may simply be too short - lengthen the hold before concluding the binding is wrong.

hazards.hazard: The early-story garage car cannot be entered
hazards.notes: At objective 'Collect the jag tip' the car in Chumbucket's garage is a prop: no prompt, R does nothing. Vehicle tests need a later save.

hazards.hazard: NumLock OFF silently changes which proxy hotkey fires
hazards.notes: With NumLock off a numpad scancode produces the navigation VK (0x51 -> VK_NEXT), and the dxgi proxy accepts navigation keys as aliases - but its alias table pairs them differently from its numpad table. A 'numpad3 = dump' press was logged as 'stereo separation -> 0.0520', i.e. it ran NUMPAD9. Worse, the stereo aliases are RIGHT and UP, which in Capture Mode MOVE THE CAMERA, so an experiment can run with a drifting viewpoint and nothing errors. Set NumLock ON first and check the logged line names the function you meant.

hazards.hazard: Six downs on the main menu lands on CREDITS, not EXIT GAME
hazards.notes: EXIT GAME is the seventh. Caught by capturing before pressing Enter.

hazards.hazard: settings.ini `keymap_group_*` values are GROUP IDS, not key codes
hazards.notes: keymap_group_enter_vehicle=17 and keymap_group_exit_vehicle=17 share a value, which no key binding could. Do not read key assignments out of these lines. V and R were established empirically instead.
